description: D-358/D-359 — the chat pilot: the FIRST WRITER of vault ns 'chat' (D-335's email-style convention: vault as-is, namespace row same-commit, retention open with a named revisit trigger) and M4's resolution wiring (D-337's deterministic-first philosophy via the SHARED classifier — no parallel resolution logic; capability names derived from the booted composition's routed ops per docs/SURFACES.md's tool-generation rule, 360 addendum A2). Conversation.principal is a plain string (D-353) — zero new authority machinery.

contract.doc: open {principal, title?} → {conversationId, rev, createdAt} — creates the conversation row (ns chat, id conv_*); principal is a plain non-empty string (user:<id>, agent:<id>, composition principals — D-353: classification is never rejection).

append {conversationId, role, content, providerId?, realizationRef?, streamRef?} → {messageId, rev, seq} — appends a message to an existing conversation (attributable refusal when it does not exist); seq is writer-assigned (index count + 1, D-378; scan fallback backfills the index); the writer-maintained per-conversation index row rides the same append critical section (bounded by CHAT_HISTORY_CAP); realizationRef ties the message to the ProviderRealization that produced it; streamRef references M1's chunk envelope when the message arrived streamed (D-352 persistence hook — ordered chunk refs → assembled content, never a separate store).

history {conversationId, limit?, principal?} → {conversation, messages, total} — bounded (CHAT_HISTORY_CAP), seq-ascending, sibling-conversation-proof history of one conversation; reads the writer-maintained index when present (O(cap) gets, D-378), legacy scan otherwise; principal? (D-379): a read under a DIFFERENT principal than the conversation's owner returns the REFUSED refusal envelope and the attempt is ledgered (meta.type=principal-refusal) — absent principal keeps the Phase-1 trusted-reader path.

resolve {conversationId, utterance, capabilities} → {decisionId, branch, kind, capability, reason, source} — M4/D-337: the deterministic half (the utterance exactly names a passed capability → rule branch, DETERMINISTIC; ledgered here as a ns-resolve ResolveDecision row) and the ambiguous half via the SHARED resolve.classify@1 (realization/human branches, the director's own ledger row). Resolution ≠ execution: the caller executes through the router and reports via resolve.report@1. capabilities is the caller-side output of contracts capabilityNamesFromRouted (the same derivation MCP tools/list consults — A2).

parser.doc: W1/T-05 harvest (D-355): the version-pinned import-parser family parser:history.import:{chatgpt|claude|gemini} — NOT routable (parser kind registers no op). The transforms are pure and deterministic: recorded export text in, ordered ParsedChunk rows out (import.conversation / import.message*n / import.done-final). Algorithms harvested from vivim-final-program@4a5eb84 src/engines/parsers/{chatgpt,claude,gemini}-import.ts (210 lines, pure) with I/O re-expressed to M1 chunk rows and the clock removed (missing timestamps land ts:0 + tsEstimated:true — a parser never calls Date.now, D-354 isolation). Transport off, recorded fixtures only (fixtures/import/). The parser produces rows only; what is WRITTEN to ns chat stays a writer's decision (W1: no chat writes beyond probe rows).

capabilities.justification: Conversation/message rows persist in the USER'S VAULT (ns 'chat') via vault.append/get/query (D-335: vault as-is, no new store); the ambiguous resolution half consults the SHARED classifier via port:resolve.classify@1 (D-337: no parallel resolution logic). The composition grants exactly these per user-signed Recipe — never this manifest. Resolution never executes the resolved capability (the caller does, through the law-gated router).
